research_questions.question: What primary-source experimental-design methods best estimate whether a learned proposal generator beats a random-admissible generator and a no-change baseline under a strictly matched total-compute envelope when proposal generation, feature/probe extraction, selection, execution, and verification are all stochastic?
research_questions.why_it_matters: A naive comparison can credit extra search/selection compute or winner-selection bias to the learned mechanism, producing a false capability-gain claim.
research_questions.closure_criterion: Identify primary methods that specify matched-cost randomized controls, paired or blocked analysis, repeated stochastic generation, and uncertainty/error control; map them to L/R/N with an explicit cost ledger and decision rule.
preferred_source_families: experimental design and randomized algorithm evaluation

research_questions.question: What minimal control set can distinguish a genuine learned-mechanism effect from cache, retained context, execution order, warm-state, or repeated-attempt effects in sequential software-agent evaluations?
research_questions.why_it_matters: If L is evaluated after additional proposal or execution work, retained state or order effects can masquerade as mechanism benefit even at nominally equal token or wall-clock budgets.
research_questions.closure_criterion: Find primary-source isolation/crossover/randomization methods and derive a machine-checkable prospective control contract covering cache/context/retention/order reset, paired seeds, and equal total resource accounting.
